statusText: The CME weekend halt still frames this assessment: nothing has quoted NQ since Friday's 21:00 UTC weekly close and nothing will until roughly 22:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, about five hours past the end of this 24-hour horizon. Tail eases one point to 10% (low), the action stays EA_ON and the status stays green, because a pathological one-way price path cannot form while no venue is quoting. What changed this hour is the first genuinely constructive item in an escalation sequence that had been one-way for two days: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei announced that Iran and Oman have agreed the geographical coordinates of a safe two-way shipping corridor through the Strait of Hormuz after three weeks of talks, with the negotiations described as positive at both political and technical level. That is a real deliverable and it trims the extreme left tail of a weekend gap. It is not a reopening, and the assessment does not treat it as one: Baghaei explicitly tied restoration of full security to the United States ending its maritime sanctions, military movements and naval blockade, and the unresolved items still include the reopening mechanism itself, maritime service fees and broader security arrangements. Tehran also repeated that no decision has been taken on resuming direct US talks, with contact still running indirectly through Qatar and Pakistan, while the 60-day window opened by the Islamabad memorandum expires on Monday. Against the diplomacy, the physical picture got worse rather than better: transits are running at roughly one vessel a day against a 130-140 peacetime norm with a seven-day average near 4.4, CENTCOM has redirected 62 commercial vessels under the blockade, and the UAE has confirmed the Friday-evening strike on an ADNOC-linked ship as a hostile Iranian attack. Stress therefore eases only one point, to 57% (elevated). The equity counterweights are unchanged and were re-verified this hour: VIX closed Friday at 14.25, less than a point above its 52-week low, and the Nasdaq-100 closed down only 0.13% to complete a third consecutive higher week. Confidence holds at 62% (solid): NQ futures, VIX, both crude benchmarks and the 2-year and 10-year yields were all re-read directly from primary quote pages this hour, and the Iran-Oman agreement was corroborated across three independent outlets.
recommendation: Action is EA_ON with a green status, derived from current Tail (10%) alone. No venue quotes NQ anywhere in the 24-hour horizon and no scheduled U.S. macro release falls inside it, so there is no basis for a directional or event-driven block in this window; existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active as always. The operative checkpoint sits just beyond the horizon at the CME reopen near 22:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, and the danger window brackets that reopen together with its first 90 minutes of price discovery - a full weekend of accumulated headlines expresses there as an opening gap, not as intraday structure. Gap risk remains genuinely two-way, and this hour it became slightly more two-way rather than less. Pulling toward relief: an Iran-Oman corridor with agreed coordinates after three weeks of technical work, talks assessed positively at both political and technical level, a White House official's statement that Trump's Hormuz territorial claim was a joke, VIX within a point of its 52-week low, and a Friday tape that absorbed the escalation with a mid-range settle rather than a liquidation. Pulling the other way: a corridor whose activation Iran has conditioned on the US lifting its blockade, an unresolved reopening mechanism, no decision on resuming direct talks with the Islamabad memorandum's 60-day window lapsing on Monday, transits down to roughly one vessel a day, 62 commercial vessels redirected by CENTCOM, a UAE-confirmed hostile strike on an ADNOC-linked ship, a Lebanon front where at least 11 were killed on Saturday and Hezbollah has promised an appropriate response it has not yet delivered, WTI at $82.40 after a +5% week and +33% year with an IEA deficit warning attached, and a 10Y at 4.696% pressing a 19-month high. Treat the reopen as a checkpoint to be scored on observed price path, not as a pre-committed direction. The dated calendar checkpoints begin with Monday's Empire State print at 12:30 UTC and culminate in the FOMC minutes at 18:00 UTC on Wednesday; the undated ones - the Treasury's Iran package and the exact hour of the negotiating-window lapse - are deliberately absent from the verified calendar because no exact time has been published.
headline: Iran and Oman agree the coordinates of a safe Hormuz shipping corridor, but Baghaei ties reopening to the US lifting its blockade while transits run at one vessel a day - Stress eases to 57%, Tail 10% with CME shut, action EA_ON.
body:
PRICE PATH (observed, stale by necessity). No venue has quoted NQ since the CME weekly close at 21:00 UTC on Friday 14 August, and none will until the Sunday reopen near 22:00 UTC on 16 August. The last live structure, re-verified this hour from the primary quote page, remains benign and unchanged: September E-mini Nasdaq-100 futures show a last print of 30,141.75, -46.75 points or -0.15% against a previous close of 30,188.50, on 397,964 contracts, opening at 30,210.75 and settling inside a 30,028.50-30,283.00 band roughly 255 points or 0.84% wide with no close pinned to either extreme. NQ sits about 2.7% below its 52-week high of 30,975.50 against a 52-week low of 22,961.50. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed at 30,046.14, -38.36 points or -0.13%, about 2.3% below its 52-week high, completing a third consecutive higher week. A two-way intraday range with a mid-range settle, several percent off the highs, is the opposite of the persistent directional efficiency, shallow pullbacks, repeated extension and pinning near extremes that the Tail definition requires. Directional efficiency here is not merely low - it is unmeasurable, because nothing has traded for more than twenty hours.

CROSS-ASSET (observed, Friday close, all re-read directly this hour). The split in the evidence remains the central fact of this assessment. Equity volatility is calm to the point of complacency: VIX closed at 14.25, -0.38 or -2.60% on the day, inside a 14.18-14.72 range and only 0.87 points above its 52-week low of 13.38 against a 52-week high of 35.30. Rates and energy say the opposite. The 10-year Treasury yield closed Friday at 4.696%, +5.5bp on the day and at the top of a 4.625-4.700% range, pressing the 52-week high of 4.747% set earlier in the week; the 2-year closed at 4.171%, +3.1bp inside a 4.098-4.178% range - a curve steepening on long-end inflation aversion rather than a growth scare. WTI stands at $82.40, +$1.15 or +1.42% on the day, +5% on the week, +3.52% on the month and +32.95% on the year; Brent at $88.52, +$1.45 or +1.67%, +34.43% on the year. Trading Economics attributes the move to Treasury Secretary Bessent's promised "unprecedented economic measures" against Iran, the continuing naval blockade of Iranian ports, Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia's Jazan refinery and an IEA warning of the widest 2026 global supply shortfall in five years, partly offset by additional Middle Eastern crude reaching U.S. markets and by vessels transiting with transponders disabled. An index within 2.3% of its high while oil is up a third on the year and the long end presses a 19-month high is a conflicted configuration, and by the risk definition a conflict of that kind belongs in Stress, not in Tail. No new megacap or semiconductor catalyst has emerged over the weekend; the next index-level corporate checkpoint, Nvidia's results on 26 August, falls outside the seven-day window.

GEOPOLITICS (new this hour, and for the first time in two days not purely one-way). The material development is procedural and constructive. Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei announced early Saturday afternoon Tehran time that Iran and Oman have agreed on a safe route for ships through the Strait of Hormuz following roughly three weeks of negotiation, with the two sides having settled the geographical coordinates of the corridor - the work having converted a southern route through Omani waters and a northern route through Iranian territorial waters into an intermediate two-way corridor - and with the talks assessed positively at both political and technical level. This is the first concrete negotiated deliverable in the sequence and it is scored as one. The qualifications are equally explicit and are why it does not move Stress further: Baghaei stated that full security in the strait cannot be restored while U.S. maritime sanctions, military movements and the naval blockade remain in place, so reopening is conditioned on American action rather than on the corridor existing; differences remain on the reopening mechanism itself, on maritime service fees and on broader security arrangements; and Tehran repeated that no decision has been taken on resuming direct talks with Washington, with contact continuing indirectly through Qatar and Pakistan, while insisting the Islamabad memorandum was meant to end the war rather than establish a temporary ceasefire. That memorandum's 60-day window expires on Monday. The physical picture meanwhile deteriorated: transits are running at roughly one vessel against a 130-140 peacetime daily norm, with a seven-day average near 4.4 or about 5% of pre-war throughput; CENTCOM has redirected 62 commercial vessels under the blockade; the UAE has confirmed the Friday-evening strike on an ADNOC-linked ship transiting the strait as a hostile Iranian attack, with no injuries reported, and has called for attacks to stop and the waterway to reopen; and UKMTO reported on Saturday that a projectile struck the hull of a bulk carrier. On Lebanon the position is unchanged in substance from last hour and remains important for what has not happened: Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon killed at least 11 people on Saturday with 19 wounded, in what the IDF described as strikes on Hezbollah infrastructure inside a security zone answering an attack that seriously wounded three Israeli soldiers; Netanyahu's office says Hezbollah violated the ceasefire and used civilians as human shields; Hezbollah has called the strikes a massacre, warned that further attacks will be met with an appropriate response and urged Beirut to abandon the negotiations - but no actual Hezbollah retaliatory fire has been reported. These were among the deadliest strikes since Lebanon agreed the U.S.-mediated framework. In Yemen, the Mocha port director reports more than 25 missiles struck the facility, killing seven, causing roughly $16 million in damage and suspending port operations.

SCORING. Tail eases one point to 10%, deep in the low band. Every ingredient the definition demands - persistent directional efficiency, shallow pullbacks, repeated extension after failed retracements, price holding near extremes - requires a live tape, and there is none; the last observed tape showed the opposite. The 10% is not a claim about structure but a price for weekend headline discontinuity expressing as a Sunday gap, and it is one point lower than last hour because an agreed corridor with settled coordinates measurably reduces the probability of the most violent class of reopening gap, even though it does not open the strait. Stress eases one point to 57% (elevated) - a deliberately small move, because the deal is conditional on the blockade being lifted, the reopening mechanism is unresolved, no direct talks are scheduled with the memorandum window lapsing Monday, and the observable throughput got worse this hour rather than better, at one transit against a 130-140 norm with a UAE-confirmed hostile strike and a bulk carrier hit. Those sit against genuine counterweights: a VIX near its 52-week low, an index that closed the week almost unchanged after a third higher week, and no actual Hezbollah retaliation despite the warning. Confidence holds at 62% (solid): this hour re-read NQ futures, VIX, WTI and Brent, and both the 2-year and 10-year yields directly from primary quote pages, and corroborated the Iran-Oman agreement and its conditions across three independent outlets; the verified seven-day calendar is carried forward from earlier direct reads, which is legitimate because dated releases cannot change over a weekend. Four fetches were refused with HTTP 403 and were replaced by other primary sources rather than left as gaps. The remaining defect is the unavoidable staleness of the price evidence. Dominant mode is mixed: complacent equity volatility against stressed rates and energy, and now constructive diplomacy against deteriorating physical throughput, is precisely a mixed regime, not a trend.

lookbackSummary: Across the trailing 24 clock-hours Tail never left the low band, running 2-11% throughout, so the action was EA_ON and the status green in every available slot. Tail held 7-9% across the back half of Friday's U.S. cash session, where the data landed and produced two-way volatility and rotation rather than directional efficiency, then printed 6% into the 21:00 UTC weekly close. Stress traced a clear event arc: 41% at 17:00 UTC on 14 August easing to 40-41% across the U.S. afternoon, then 34% at the close. The two runs immediately after the close scored the halt itself at Tail 2% and Stress 12%; from 00:00 UTC onward that reading was corrected back to Tail 9% and Stress 45% on the judgement that a shut venue does not neutralise a live Hormuz closure, and 45% then held for six consecutive hours through 05:00 UTC. From 06:00 UTC the weekend escalation sequence lifted the series steadily - Tail to 10% and then 11%, Stress through 48%, 50%, 51%, 52%, 53%, 54%, 55%, 56% and 58% - as the Mocha barrage, the Lebanon strikes, the ADNOC vessel attack, the U.S. territorial claim, Hezbollah's retaliation warning, Gharibabadi's blockade-until-defeat statement and Araghchi's confirmation that no talks are being held landed one after another with no tape to absorb them. The series peaked at Tail 11% and Stress 58% in the 16:00 UTC slot, immediately before this hour's Iran-Oman corridor agreement. Confidence ran 36-62%, weakest in the hours immediately around the weekly close and improving steadily from 57% to 62% across the weekend halt as each dimension was re-verified hour by hour. The 20:00 UTC slot on 14 August is unavailable because no successful Claude snapshot was published for that hour; those fields are null and no past opinion has been rewritten.
outlookSummary: The entire 24-hour horizon falls inside the CME weekend halt - it runs from 17:00 UTC on Saturday 15 August to 16:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, ending roughly five hours before the reopen near 22:00 UTC that day - so neither a scheduled U.S. macro release nor a tradable price path falls within it. Tail is projected flat at 10% through the remaining Saturday evening slots, stepping to 11% from 22:00 UTC and to 12% from Sunday morning as the reopen edges into view; those increments reflect accumulating gap risk, not observed structure, and every slot stays deep in the low band, so the action is EA_ON and the status green throughout. Stress is projected to hold at 57% through the thin Saturday hours when weekend headline flow is historically lightest, firming to 58% overnight and to 59% across Sunday midday as the unresolved threads converge on the reopen and on Monday's lapse of the Islamabad memorandum's 60-day window. Confidence drifts from 62% to 55% across the horizon as the last live prints age further without replacement. The material catalyst sits just beyond the horizon: the CME reopen and its first 90 minutes of price discovery, which the danger window brackets, and which is now also the last liquid session before that window expires. Inside the horizon the realistic risks are headline-driven and, unusually for this sequence, they cut both ways - a U.S. response to the Iran-Oman corridor or any movement on the blockade condition would be constructive, while an actual Hezbollah retaliation converting a warning that has so far produced no fire, a further Hormuz vessel strike, an early leak of the Treasury's Iran package, or a formal statement on the lapsing memorandum would not. Each would move Stress and the expected gap rather than produce observable one-way structure. The first scheduled checkpoint is Monday's Empire State print at 12:30 UTC; the week's highest-impact dated items are Tuesday's housing and industrial production data, the FOMC minutes at 18:00 UTC on Wednesday 19 August, Thursday's claims and Philadelphia Fed pair, and Friday's S&P Global flash PMIs. Its highest-impact undated items are the Treasury's Iran package and the precise hour at which the negotiating window lapses, both omitted from the calendar because no exact time has been published. Nvidia's results on 26 August and the Jackson Hole symposium later that month both fall outside this seven-day window.
